events.comment:
At each frame, the camera must catchup the target by a given ratio (speed)
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - 1) - targetX) * (1 - speed)

The frame rate must not impact on the catch-up speed, we don't want a speed in ratio per frame but a speed ratio per second, like this:
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - 1s) - targetX) * (1 - speed)

Ok, but we still need to process each frame, we can use a exponent for this:
cameraX(t) - targetX = (cameraX(t - timeDelta) - targetX) * (1 - speed)^timeDelta
cameraX(t) = targetX + (cameraX(t - timeDelta) - targetX) * exp(timeDelta * ln((1 - speed)))

pow is probably more efficient than precalculated log if the speed is changed continuously but this might be rare enough.

eventsFunctionsExtensions.name: SpriteMultitouchJoystick
description: Multitouch joysticks are objects showing a joystick on the screen, useful for mobile. They work like a physical gamepad:
- 4 or 8 directions
- Analogus pads
- Player selection

- Automatic "mapper" behaviors for 2D and 3D movement behaviors (platformer characters, top-down movement, 3D character etc...). Add one of these to the object with the movement behavior (i.e: the player most of the time) and the behavior will then be controlled automatically by the virtual joystick (it works by reading the multitouch joystick state and simulating controls). No need for additional events to make it work once the behaviors are set up.
There are ready-to-use joysticks in the asset-store [multitouch joysticks pack](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?initial-dialog=asset-store&asset-pack=multitouch-joysticks-multitouch-joysticks).

eventsFunctionsExtensions.shortDescription: A ground with hills and valleys that can be sculpted and painted in the editor, with collisions.
description: A 3D terrain object for open worlds, adventure or racing games: hills, mountains, islands or valleys, with painted layers of grass, dirt, rock or sand.
- **Sculpt and paint in the scene editor**: select a terrain to show the tools (raise, lower, smooth, flatten and paint 4 layers).
- **Start from a relief** (hills, mountains, island) or **from a heightmap image**.
- **Steep slopes automatically show rock** (or any layer).

- **Natural borders between layers**: stones and tufts of a texture cover the gaps of the other where layers meet (height blending), and the repetition of textures is made less visible (texture variation).
- **Physics**: add the **3D physics** behavior to the terrain. Characters and objects collide with the ground exactly. The terrain is always static.

- **Pathfinding**: add the **floor/obstacle for pathfinding (navmesh based)** behavior to the terrain, so that characters with the navmesh pathfinding behavior walk on its hills and around its cliffs (in recent GDevelop versions).

- **Shape it with the Edits property**: a list of raise, flatten, smooth and paint strokes written in JSON, shown in the scene editor. It's readable and can be changed by hand or by an AI agent, like the relief, the heightmap and the other properties. Actions only change the terrain during the game.
- **Change it during the game** with actions (raise, lower, flatten, smooth, paint, along a line for paths and rivers) and read the ground height, slope or layer with expressions.

- **Grass**: add a **terrain grass** object over the terrain. Thousands of blades sway in the wind, grow where a layer (like grass) is painted and where the ground is not too steep, and are pushed aside by characters. Sculpt or paint the terrain and the grass follows.

- **Forests, rocks and bushes**: add a **scattered models** object over the terrain. It places hundreds or thousands of copies of a 3D model (trees, rocks, bushes, flowers...) on the ground and draws them all at once, which is much faster than an object for each. Copies grow where a layer is painted, away from steep slopes, and follow the ground when it's sculpted. Add or erase them with the brushes of the scene editor or with the Edits property, give trees trunk collisions, and cut them down with actions. Ready-made forests, rocks and bushes are in the asset store.

- **Tunnels and caves**: make holes in the ground (and fill them again) with the brushes, the Edits property or actions, and put a 3D model of the tunnel or the cave (with a mesh collision shape) under the ground. Nothing is drawn in holes, and characters, cars and rays go through them.
- **Made for large worlds**: the terrain is split in chunks that are hidden when off-screen and simplified when far away, and collisions are updated only where the ground changes.

propertyDescriptors.description: Optional. Replaces the relief: black is the lowest, white the highest (the object depth).

propertyDescriptors.label: Edits
propertyDescriptors.description: Changes of the relief or heightmap, applied in order, as a JSON list, for example [{"tool": "raise", "x": 0.3, "y": 0.4, "radius": 0.15, "height": 0.4}, {"tool": "paint", "x": 0.1, "y": 0.9, "toX": 0.8, "toY": 0.2, "radius": 0.02, "layer": 2}]. Tools: raise (height added to the ground, negative to lower), flatten (z: the ground is brought to this height, fully at the center, cutting what is above it and filling what is below; with toX and toY, toZ gives the height at the end of the line, for a road going up), smooth (strength), paint (layer, from 1 to 4, and strength), tint (color, like "120;140;60", multiplying the layers, white removing the tint, and strength), wetness (amount, from 0 for dry to 1 for wet, and strength), hole (no ground in the radius, for the entrances of tunnels and caves) and fill (the holes in the radius are filled with the layers of the ground around them). x, y and radius are fractions (0 to 1) of the terrain size (x is (scene X - terrain X) / terrain width). height and z are fractions of its depth: the ground at z is at Z = terrain Z + z * terrain depth. Add toX and toY to change the ground along a line (paths, rivers, ridges). Shown in the scene editor.
propertyDescriptors.name: Edits

propertyDescriptors.label: Resolution

propertyDescriptors.description: Where copies are added or erased, applied in order, as a JSON list, for example [{"tool": "add", "x": 0.3, "y": 0.4, "radius": 0.15}, {"tool": "erase", "x": 0.1, "y": 0.9, "toX": 0.8, "toY": 0.2, "radius": 0.02}].
